result.summary: The image shows a wide, multi-lane arterial road with a marked high-visibility crosswalk and a small concrete refuge island. While basic pedestrian infrastructure like sidewalks and signals are present, the long crossing distance and high-speed road design create a challenging environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross at least four travel lanes plus turn lanes, increasing exposure time to vehicle traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Inadequate Refuge Island
hazards.description: The concrete refuge island is very narrow and lacks protective bollards or significant width to safely accommodate multiple pedestrians or those with mobility devices.

hazards.name: Pavement Degradation
hazards.description: Visible longitudinal cracking in the asphalt within the intersection area could present a trip hazard or affect vehicle braking.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane or unused roadway area to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Enhanced Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Widen the median refuge and add 'nose' protection to better shield pedestrians waiting to cross the second half of the street.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles get a green light.
